description: The source families this package actually walked, with members inspected vs members known.

evidence.note: Directory paginates via ?wpv_paged=N query params (WordPress Views/WPV plugin), 6 pages of ~10 venues each
Final (6th) page confirmed only 4 further venues, closing out the full member count at 54

families.notes: Walked all 6 paginated pages and fetched each of the 54 individual member profile pages for stated capacity figures. Contrary to Package 05's note that this directory needed a browser for JS pagination, WebFetch alone successfully traversed every page via the wpv_paged URL query parameter (server-side WordPress Views pagination, not a client-only JS barrier) -- a playwright browser session was opened but proved unnecessary once this was discovered. Of 54 members, 4 stated a specific, identifiable room/hall with capacity >=1000 not already held by Package 05 (Ivor Crewe Lecture Hall/Event Essex, Kent Sports Centre, Maxwell Hall/Salford, Central Hall/York) -- emitted to new-venues.jsonl with capacity corroborated against each university's own official conferencing site. Several other members stated vague, non-room-specific aggregate figures (e.g. 'accommodating over 2,000 delegates throughout the year' for Portsmouth, 'capacities ranging from 4-2000 guests' for Leeds, 'up to 1000 delegates' for Nottingham Venues) that could not be tied to one specific room and were not treated as capacity evidence for a single venue -- these are honest non-findings, not omissions. Three members' largest room was already held by Package 05 under a different label (Great Hall, University of Birmingham; McEwan Hall, Edinburgh; Sport Central, Northumbria) and were not re-emitted.

evidence.note: Fetched page states '57 matching venues total across 2 pages, currently showing page 1 of 2' -- page 1's 30 venues (with stated capacities) were retrieved; page 2 could not be retrieved (the ?page=2 query parameter returned identical page-1 content on refetch, indicating client-side/JS-driven pagination that plain fetching could not traverse)

Cross-checking the 30 inspected venues against the existing estate found no unheld >=1000 candidate that survived scrutiny -- all either already held, non-UK (Aviva Stadium, Dublin), or describe conference/event capacity below 1,000 for an already-held sports venue (e.g. Harlequins/Twickenham Stoop 910, Edgbaston Stadium 1,050 -- both already held under their sports-ground identity). Page 2 (remaining 27 members) genuinely unreached -- residual gap, not falsely claimed as checked.

Scanning the visible names surfaced two genuine leads that were followed up and confirmed elsewhere in this package's output: 'ACC Liverpool' (-> Convention Centre, Liverpool Experience Campus, new-venues.jsonl) and multiple already-held venues (Aintree Racecourse & Conference Centre, Alton Towers Resort, Barbican Centre, Manchester Central, NEC Group Ltd, Royal Armouries). venue-sitemap.xml enumerates exactly 53 individual /venue/ URLs -- fetched in full and used as the complete member list

families.notes: Package 05 had spot-checked ~18 of 53 known member URLs from this sitemap. Fetched and recorded a stated capacity for all 53, completing the remaining ~35 unchecked. Two candidates initially appeared to reach >=1000 on the VoE profile page itself (Unique Venues Birmingham / Library of Birmingham 'Level 2 Library Feature Space' at 1,000 reception; Hellidon Lakes Hotel 'Top Field' at 1000 theatre) but neither survived cross-checking against independent sources: official/third-party sources for Library of Birmingham cap out at 550 banqueting and The Rep's House auditorium at ~800-825, and independent listings for Hellidon Lakes cap its largest bookable room at 300 delegates with no corroboration anywhere of a 1000-capacity 'Top Field'. Per the brief's rule that a single uncorroborated figure is not sufficient capacity evidence, neither was promoted to new-venues.jsonl -- recorded here as a genuine non-finding, not an omission. One member (University of Birmingham Conferences & Events / Great Hall) independently corroborated Package 05's existing 1,000-theatre-style figure for the already-held 'Great Hall, University of Birmingham'. No other VoE member's stated capacity reached 1,000 in any configuration; this consortium's roster is materially smaller-scale (boardrooms, training centres, hotel suites, country-house hotels) than Academic Venue Solutions or the major national conference/exhibition operators.

researcher_coverage_statements.package_06_action: Walked Academic Venue Solutions (54 members) and Venues of Excellence/Conference Centres of Excellence (53 members) in full, checking every member's stated capacity; cross-checked national DMO business-events sites (VisitScotland, Meet in Wales, Visit Belfast); confirmed 2 new conference centres: National Conference Centre (Solihull, 1,400 theatre) and New Dock Hall, Royal Armouries (Leeds, 1,500 reception) -- the latter discovered while re-checking Leeds's principal conference estate for the CONVENTION_CENTRE pass and confirmed to be a physically distinct, adjacent building from the already-held Royal Armouries Hall inside the museum.

researcher_coverage_statements.residual_gap: The two named consortium/directory estates (AVS, VoE) were walked exhaustively member-by-member; national DMO sites were checked but not exhaustively -- a residual seam of smaller regional/city-council-run conference centres not carried by any of these consortia may still exist uncounted, but no further discoverable estate was identified.

researcher_coverage_statements.package_06_action: Checked every major UK city (London, Birmingham, Manchester, Liverpool, Glasgow, Edinburgh, Cardiff, Belfast, Newcastle/Gateshead, Leeds, Sheffield, Bristol, Nottingham, Bournemouth, Brighton, Harrogate, Torquay, Telford, Southampton, Plymouth -- 20 cities) for a principal convention/congress facility, confirming one genuine gap (Liverpool -- resolved in the prior pass) and two cities that genuinely lack one today: Newcastle/Gateshead's planned 'Sage' arena/ICC has not begun construction, and Bristol's planned Aviva Arena (formerly YTL Arena) began construction in 2026 but is not due to open before 2028 at the earliest -- both correctly excluded as not-yet-existing, following the same discipline as the Southport near-miss.
researcher_coverage_statements.residual_gap: Bristol and Newcastle/Gateshead are a genuinely bounded, explicit gap: neither city has an operating purpose-built convention centre as of this research (both have funded, named projects years from opening). Separately, a taxonomy note rather than a coverage gap: Glasgow (SEC), Edinburgh (EICC), Cardiff (ICC Wales) and Belfast (ICC Belfast) each already have their principal convention facility held in the census, just classified as MULTI_PURPOSE_VENUE rather than CONVENTION_CENTRE by Package 05's own existing convention -- not re-classified here since that is outside this researcher's remit, but flagged so the low raw CONVENTION_CENTRE count is not mistaken for a coverage gap in those four cities.

researcher_coverage_statements.package_06_action: Resolved all 6 EXHIBITION_CENTRE rows in the assigned capacity-unverified list (Task 3) via official/high-quality-third-party fetched evidence: Farnborough International, Great Yorkshire Events Centre, NAEC Stoneleigh and Exhibition Centre Liverpool all confirmed >=1000; Royal Cornwall Events Centre confirmed via annual-show attendance; Staffordshire County Showground (Bingley Hall) genuinely unresolved after repeated attempts.
source_families_checked: Direct official-site research per assigned row
researcher_coverage_statements.residual_gap: Staffordshire County Showground / Bingley Hall's person-capacity figure could not be pinned to a fetched source (only floor-area figures were found); no broader national exhibition-centre estate sweep beyond the assigned rows and the AVS/VoE consortium checks was attempted.

researcher_coverage_statements.package_06_action: Walked Academic Venue Solutions (all 54 members, including its full 6-page paginated directory) member-by-member for capacity; cross-checked against Package05's 7 already-held rows; confirmed 4 new venues (Ivor Crewe Lecture Hall/Essex, Kent Sports Centre, Maxwell Hall/Salford, Central Hall/York) via each university's own official site; resolved the assigned Surrey Sports Park unverified row as genuinely conflicting/unresolved.
researcher_coverage_statements.residual_gap: AVS's ~54 members were the only national consortium found for this class and were checked exhaustively; individual universities not in AVS/VoE membership (e.g. Russell Group members that run their own independent conferencing brand) were not swept individually beyond what AVS/VoE already covered -- a residual seam of non-consortium university venues may exist.

Cross-checked an independent ranking of the UK's largest hotel ballrooms overall (InterContinental O2 Arora Ballroom, Hilton London Metropole, Grosvenor House Great Room) -- confirmed the top of this market is now fully represented in the census (all three held; Grosvenor House added in the prior pass). Spot-checked regional flagship conference hotels: Hilton Liverpool (450, below), the Midland Hotel Manchester (700, below).
source_families_checked: Ad hoc ranking of UK's largest hotel ballrooms
Business Events Belfast and Northern Ireland (discovery only)
researcher_coverage_statements.residual_gap: Two full operator estates (De Vere, QHotels -- together ~41 properties) were walked and confirmed to specialise in mid-size country-house conferencing well below the 1,000 threshold, and the small, well-documented top tier of UK hotel ballrooms is now fully represented. Residual gap, named and bounded: Scottish/NI resort hotels surfaced as leads but not individually capacity-checked (Gleneagles, Trump Turnberry, Fairmont St Andrews, Dalmahoy, Crowne Plaza Belfast) and Hilton Manchester Deansgate's Deansgate Suite (capacity not found stated anywhere).

researcher_coverage_statements.package_06_action: Two-pass discovery search (no national directory exists for this class, confirmed independently in both passes) across ~25 named town halls/guildhalls/corn exchanges/assembly rooms: confirmed 2 new civic halls (Albert Halls Bolton 1,000 standing; Ipswich Corn Exchange 1,076 seated). Below-threshold and ruled out: Leeds Civic Hall (220), Wakefield Town Hall (186), Rochdale Town Hall (500), Oxford Town Hall (500), London Guildhall Great Hall (900), Edinburgh Assembly Rooms Music Hall (788), Northampton Guildhall (440). Checked major civic/leisure trusts running city-wide venue estates (Glasgow Life, Aberdeen Performing Arts, GLL/Better) and confirmed their flagship large halls (Glasgow Royal Concert Hall 2,475; Aberdeen Music Hall 1,281) are already held under CONCERT_HALL, not an additional CIVIC_HALL gap. Checked Derby Assembly Rooms: confirmed disused since 2014 and being demolished, not a live candidate -- its intended functional replacement (a new Becketwell venue) is the same building already resolved and held as Vaillant Live (ARENA, 3,500) in Task 3, so no double-counting risk. Also independently re-confirmed (without re-adding) that Preston Guild Hall and King George's Hall Blackburn, both already held under other classes, remain correctly classified.
source_families_checked: Ad hoc web search of major UK town halls/guildhalls/corn exchanges (two passes)
researcher_coverage_statements.residual_gap: Confirmed across two research passes that no national member directory or consortium exists for this class -- Package 05's original note stands and is now independently re-verified, which is itself the bounding fact the brief asked for. Coverage is therefore name-by-name discovery across ~25 major regional town halls/guildhalls/corn exchanges/trusts rather than estate-walking. Explicitly NOT checked: smaller-city (population <150k) town halls not named in either pass, on the reasonable, stated (not silently assumed) basis that every one actually checked in this class capped out at 200-900 except the 2 confirmed finds -- a genuine residual, not a claim of exhaustive national verification. Colchester's Albert Hall's capacity was never found stated anywhere and remains a named, unresolved lead.

researcher_coverage_statements.package_06_action: Completed a genuine source-estate pass: walked the resident-orchestra home-venue circuit for every full-time UK symphony/philharmonic orchestra (LSO-Barbican, LPO & Philharmonia-Royal Festival Hall, RPO-Cadogan Hall, CBSO-Symphony Hall, Halle-Bridgewater Hall, RLPO-Liverpool Philharmonic Hall, BBC SSO & RSNO-Glasgow Royal Concert Hall, Ulster Orchestra-Ulster Hall, BBC NOW-St David's Hall, Bournemouth SO-Lighthouse Poole) -- every single one is already held in the census except Cadogan Hall (953 seats, confirmed below threshold via a direct Wikipedia infobox fetch). Cross-checked major city-council/charitable cultural-trust estates (Glasgow Life, Aberdeen Performing Arts, OnFife) and confirmed their flagship halls are already held, not gaps. Also checked (prior + this pass) Royal Hall Harrogate (978), Eden Court Empire Theatre Inverness (840), Buxton Opera House (902) -- all below threshold -- and investigated Southport's Marine Lake Events Centre and Gateshead's 'Sage' project in detail, correctly excluding both as not-yet-operating.
source_families_checked: Ad hoc web search of major UK concert halls by capacity
researcher_coverage_statements.residual_gap: The national orchestral circuit -- the single most authoritative source-estate for this class, since it is exactly 'the venues the major UK orchestras actually tour to/are resident at' -- is fully checked and closed: every full-time UK orchestra's home hall is either already held or (Cadogan Hall only) confirmed below threshold, with zero new confirmed venues because the circuit was already comprehensively held by Package 05. Residual gap is bounded to independent, non-orchestra-affiliated concert halls in smaller cities not individually swept (the same residual class as CIVIC_HALL) -- no further nationally material estate (Arts Council England does not publish a usable 'major venues' portfolio list; none was found) was identified.

Per-course capacity_context recorded honestly: most operators publish no capacity figure at all (confirmed absence, not a failed search); a handful publish attendance ranges (Salisbury 2,000-9,000; Fakenham up to 4,500+) or marketing/record attendance claims (Chester, Chelmsford City ~20,000+; Doncaster 60,000 St Leger 2026 record; Epsom 28,000 Derby Day 2026 record) which were used as MEDIUM-confidence evidence, explicitly labelled as attendance/record figures rather than stated formal capacities. CORRECTION APPLIED mid-task per coordinator review: Ffos Las was originally miscoded CONFIRMED_1000_PLUS on a circa-2009 PLANNED/proposed capacity figure alone; this has been corrected to CAPACITY_STILL_UNVERIFIED_HIGH_VALUE_CANDIDATE since a planned figure is not evidence of current capacity. Doncaster was upgraded from a Wikipedia-only figure (50,000) to the operator's own more recent 2026 record-attendance figure (60,000, OFFICIAL_OPERATOR). Follow-up operator-page fetches were also made for Epsom (corroborating record added), York and Hamilton Park (both checked, genuinely carry no usable current figure, Wikipedia sourcing retained) and Aintree/Cheltenham (both timed out twice, residual gap, Wikipedia sourcing retained).
